```ts
import { Order } from './types';

export function compareOrders(a: Order, b: Order): number {
  if (a.createdAt < b.createdAt) return -1;
  if (a.createdAt > b.createdAt) return 1;
  if (a.id < b.id) return -1;
  if (a.id > b.id) return 1;

}
```

```ts
// src/repository.ts
import { Order } from './types';

export interface Cursor { createdAt: string; id: string }

export function parseCursor(cursor: string | null | undefined): Cursor | null {
  if (cursor === undefined || cursor === null) return null;
  if (typeof cursor !== 'string') throw new Error('invalid request');
  const parts = cursor.split('|');
  if (parts.length !== 2 || parts[0].length === 0 || parts[1].length === 0) {
    throw new Error('invalid request');
  }
  return { createdAt: parts[0], id: parts[1] };
}

export function compareOrders(a: Order, b: Order): number {
  if (a.createdAt !== b.createdAt) return a.createdAt < b.createdAt ? -1 : 1;
  if (a.id !== b.id) return a.id < b.id ? -1 : 1;
  return 0;
}

export class OrderRepository {
  constructor(private readonly rows: Order[]) {}

  list(tenant: string, cursor?: string | null, limit?: number): Order[] {
    const parsed = parseCursor(cursor);
    let items = this.rows
      .filter(row => row.tenant === tenant)
      .sort(compareOrders); // filter returns a fresh array

    if (parsed !== null) {
      const { createdAt, id } = parsed;
      items = items.filter(order =>
        order.createdAt > createdAt ||
        (order.createdAt === createdAt && order.id > id)
      );
    }

    if (limit !== undefined && Number.isInteger(limit) && limit >= 0) {
      items = items.slice(0, limit);
    }

    return items;
  }
}
```

```ts
import { Order } from './types';

interface CursorPosition {
  createdAt: string;
  id: string;
}

/**
 * Parses `createdAt + '|' + id` cursor. IDs and dates never contain '|',
 * so the cursor must split into exactly two nonempty parts.
 */
export function parseCursor(cursor: unknown): CursorPosition | null {
  if (cursor === undefined || cursor === null) return null;
  if (typeof cursor !== 'string') throw new Error('invalid request');
  const parts = cursor.split('|');
  if (parts.length !== 2 || parts[0].length === 0 || parts[1].length === 0) {
    throw new Error('invalid request');
  }
  return { createdAt: parts[0], id: parts[1] };
}

export function compareOrders(a: Order, b: Order): number {
  if (a.createdAt !== b.createdAt) return a.createdAt < b.createdAt ? -1 : 1;
  if (a.id !== b.id) return a.id < b.id ? -1 : 1;
  return 0;
}

export class OrderRepository {
  constructor(private readonly rows: Order[]) {}

  list(tenant: string, cursor?: string | null, limit?: number): Order[] {
    const position = parseCursor(cursor);

    // filter() returns a fresh array, so sorting it never mutates `this.rows`.
    let items = this.rows.filter(row => row.tenant === tenant).sort(compareOrders);

    if (position !== null) {
      items = items.filter(order =>
        order.createdAt > position.createdAt ||
        (order.createdAt === position.createdAt && order.id > position.id)
      );
    }

    if (limit !== undefined && Number.isInteger(limit) && limit >= 0) {
      items = items.slice(0, limit);
    }

    return items;
  }
}
```

## Summary

Cursor pagination was added to the order listing while preserving the existing interfaces' backward compatibility.

### `src/repository.ts`
- Added `compareOrders(a, b)`: ascending by `createdAt`, then `id` via plain lexicographic (`<`/`>`) string comparison.
- Added `parseCursor(cursor)`: accepts `undefined`/`null` as "no cursor"; a non-string or a string that doesn't split into exactly two nonempty `|`-separated parts throws `Error('invalid request')`.
- Extended `OrderRepository.list(tenant, cursor?, limit?)` (existing `list(tenant)` callers unchanged) to:
  1. filter by tenant first,
  2. sort a fresh array — `filter()` already returns a new array, so the constructor's input array and rows are never mutated,
  3. resume **strictly after** the `(createdAt, id)` position via pair comparison (`createdAt > c || (createdAt === c && id > c)`), which naturally works when the cursor row was deleted or belongs to another tenant,
  4. optionally slice to `limit`.

### `src/handler.ts`
- Validates `tenant` (nonempty string), `limit` (integer 1–100), and the cursor via `parseCursor`, all throwing `Error('invalid request')`.
- Fetches tenant-filtered, sorted, cursor-resumed rows from the repository, cuts the page to `limit`, and returns `nextCursor` as `createdAt|id` of the last returned item when a further matching order exists, otherwise `null`.

`src/types.ts` needed no change — `Page` already declared `nextCursor: string | null`.

### Checks
Added `checks/cursor.cjs` covering: multi-page walks with equal-date/lexicographic-id boundaries (no repeats/skips), deleted cursor rows, cross-tenant cursors with filter-before-pagination, exact-page and empty-result `null` cursors, all validation cases, repository direct use, and input non-mutation. Also ran a 1000-trial randomized property test (page concatenation equals the full sorted filtered list, input unchanged) — all passed.

`tsc -p tsconfig.json && node checks/public.cjs` passes; the new cursor checks also pass.
